hints: Focus on what cooling does to molecular energies, most molecules slow down so the whole distribution squeezes to the left.
Remember the two key shape rules for a lower temperature, the peak gets taller and moves left, while the high energy tail drops.
Compare X on the left slope with Y at the old peak and Z on the right slope to see which points end up under a taller or shorter curve.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the Boltzmann curve shows**

Think of it as a snapshot of how energy is shared out. The x-axis is molecular energy and the y-axis, $n$, is how many molecules have that energy.

Key rule: area under the curve = total number of molecules, so it stays constant.

**Apply the effect of lower temperature**

Cooling from $50^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $40^{\circ}\text{C}$ gives molecules less average kinetic energy. The distribution shifts left toward lower energy.

Shape change: peak becomes taller and narrower, high-energy tail becomes lower:
$$\text{lower } T \rightarrow \text{taller, narrower peak shifted left}$$

**Check X, Y and Z one by one**

X is low energy on the left slope. The new taller, left-shifted curve sits above the old curve there, so $n$ at X is higher.

Y is the old peak and Z is higher energy on the right slope. The new curve has moved left and flattened on the right, so both points now sit under a lower part of the curve, so $n$ at Y and Z is lower.

options.A: X higher and Y lower is correct, but Z higher is wrong. Cooling reduces the number of high energy molecules, so the right hand tail must fall, not rise. This choice confuses the taller peak with a rise everywhere.
options.B: This is correct. Lower temperature shifts the distribution left and makes it taller and narrower. More molecules now have low energy X, so n rises, while fewer molecules have peak energy Y and high energy Z, so n falls at both.
options.C: This describes heating, not cooling. A higher temperature would lower the peak and push molecules to higher energy, giving lower X and higher tail. Here temperature is reduced, so the opposite happens.
options.D: Y lower and Z lower is correct, but X lower is wrong. The total area must stay the same, so if high energy numbers fall, low energy numbers must rise. The new curve is taller on the left, so n at X increases.
